title: "Remote control requested" dialog shows up after clicking on the tray icon of certain apps
line: Clicking the tray icon of GTK3, Electron and other legacy apps no longer pops up a "Remote Control" permission dialog; the click just reaches the app.
explanation: For legacy XEmbed tray icons that don't select button events (GTK3, Electron, some Java apps), xembedsniproxy replays the click with XTest. On Wayland Xwayland forwards XTest through libei to KWin, which can't verify which X11 client is asking and shows its "plasma-kded6-x11 is asking to control input devices" prompt; without Allow the click is lost. The proxy now opens its own libei connection to KWin through KWin's org.kde.KWin.EIS.RemoteDesktop D-Bus interface (the one the portal uses, no prompt) and sends the button and scroll events there, using the same button mapping as Xwayland; XTest stays as the fallback on X11, without libei at build time, or when KWin has no EIS.

commits.message:
xembed-sni-proxy: inject clicks through KWin instead of XTest on Wayland

On Wayland, Xwayland turns XTest events into a libei connection that
KWin has to ask the user about, so clicking a GTK3 or Electron tray icon
showed a remote control prompt. Send these clicks through KWin's EIS.

BUG: 490666

media.caption: Master: left-clicking a GTK3 tray icon in the panel opens the Remote Control prompt, and the app gets nothing
With the fix: the same click opens the app's window directly, no prompt
With the fix: two left clicks and a right click on the tray icon, each reaching the app (window, then its context menu), no prompt
